- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a recent spike (e.g., >70.5), model often overshoots and forecasts too high; cap forecast at +1.5–2.0% above recent peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% relative to recent mean or add sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- Model consistently underpredicts mean-reversion zones (e.g., below 65–66) — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment shifts — adjust for 1–2 day delay in reaction to sentiment changes, especially if sentiment turns sharply.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/–0.3), model overfits short-term noise; use 3–5 day smoothing or sentiment-weighted moving average to dampen noise.
